symbols.name: \(n\)
symbols.def: Common sample size in each randomized treatment arm.

symbols.name: \(m\)
symbols.def: Fold size \(m=n/2\).

symbols.name: \(i\)
symbols.def: Unit index within an arm.

symbols.name: \(d\)
symbols.def: Dimension of the conditioning covariate; \(d=0\) denotes the no-covariate branch.

symbols.name: \(s_y\)
symbols.def: H\"older smoothness in the outcome coordinate.

symbols.name: \(s_z\)
symbols.def: H\"older smoothness in the covariate coordinates when \(d\ge1\).

symbols.name: \(\alpha\)
symbols.def: Nominal noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: \(c\)
symbols.def: Uniform density lower bound.

symbols.name: \(C\)
symbols.def: Uniform density upper bound.

symbols.name: \(L\)
symbols.def: Radius of each anisotropic H\"older ball.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal A\)
symbols.def: Treatment-arm index set.

symbols.name: \(a\)
symbols.def: Treatment-arm index.

symbols.name: \(e\)
symbols.def: Evaluation-fold index; the other fold is the pilot fold.

symbols.name: \(I_{a,e}\)
symbols.def: Deterministic fold \(e\) in arm \(a\), of cardinality \(m\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal Y\)
symbols.def: Scalar outcome support.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal Z_d\)
symbols.def: Covariate support for \(d\ge1\); for \(d=0\), \(\mathcal Z_0\) is a singleton.

symbols.name: \(y\)
symbols.def: Outcome argument.

symbols.name: \(z\)
symbols.def: Covariate argument.

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: Generic discrepancy direction with zero integral in the outcome coordinate at every covariate value.

symbols.name: \(b\)
symbols.def: Generic bounded covariate amplitude in the cosine second-variation calculation.

symbols.name: \(P_{a,n}\)
symbols.def: Law of the observed outcome and covariate in arm \(a\) at index \(n\).

symbols.name: \(Y_n(a)\)
symbols.def: Potential outcome under arm \(a\), with marginal law induced by \(P_{a,n}\).

symbols.name: \(Y_{a,i,n}\)
symbols.def: Outcome coordinate of observation \(i\) in arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(Z_{a,i,n}\)
symbols.def: Covariate coordinate of observation \(i\) in arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(W_{a,i,n}\)
symbols.def: Observation \(W_{a,i,n}=(Y_{a,i,n},Z_{a,i,n})\) from arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(R_n\)
symbols.def: Common covariate marginal of the two arm laws.

symbols.name: \(r_n\)
symbols.def: Lebesgue density of \(R_n\) for \(d\ge1\), and the constant one for \(d=0\).

symbols.name: \(Q_{a,n}\)
symbols.def: Conditional law of the outcome given the covariate in arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(q_{a,n}\)
symbols.def: Conditional density defined by \(Q_{a,n}(dy\mid z)=q_{a,n}(y,z)dy\).

symbols.name: \(\bar q_n\)
symbols.def: Reference density \(\bar q_n=(q_{0,n}+q_{1,n})/2\).

symbols.name: \(\Delta_n\)
symbols.def: Conditional-law discrepancy \(\Delta_n=q_{1,n}-q_{0,n}\), which integrates to zero in \(y\) at every \(z\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal G_{n,z}\)
symbols.def: Weighted Neumann inverse: \(u=\mathcal G_{n,z}h\) solves \(-\partial_y(\bar q_n(y,z)\partial_yu(y))=h(y)\), \(\partial_yu(0)=\partial_yu(1)=0\), and \(\int_0^1u(y)dy=0\).

symbols.name: \(\rho_n\)
symbols.def: Inverse-elliptic separation defined by \(\rho_n^2=\int\Delta_n(y,z)(\mathcal G_{n,z}\Delta_n(\cdot,z))(y)dydR_n(z)\).

symbols.name: \(\rho\)
symbols.def: Radius of a local neighborhood of conditional equality.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\)
symbols.def: Local anisotropic conditional-transport model class declared in the definitions array.

symbols.name: \(\theta_n\)
symbols.def: Conditional quadratic transport endpoint \(\theta_n=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}W_2^2(Q_{0,n}(\cdot\mid z),Q_{1,n}(\cdot\mid z))dR_n(z)\), the sharp lower endpoint of \(E[(Y_n(1)-Y_n(0))^2]\) over conditional couplings.

symbols.name: \(\Psi_y\)
symbols.def: Compactly supported boundary-corrected outcome wavelets, with the constant removed from discrepancy projections.

symbols.name: \(\Psi_z\)
symbols.def: Tensor boundary-corrected covariate wavelets when \(d\ge1\), and the singleton constant basis when \(d=0\).

symbols.name: \(J_y\)
symbols.def: Outcome resolution.

symbols.name: \(J_z\)
symbols.def: Covariate resolution, used only when \(d\ge1\).

symbols.name: \(J_y^*\)
symbols.def: Rate-balancing outcome resolution for the conditional branch.

symbols.name: \(J_z^*\)
symbols.def: Rate-balancing covariate resolution for the conditional branch.

symbols.name: \(J_y^0\)
symbols.def: Growing outcome resolution for the no-covariate branch.

symbols.name: \(\bar J_y\)
symbols.def: Outcome resolution of each opposite-fold pilot density estimator.

symbols.name: \(\bar J_z\)
symbols.def: Covariate resolution of each opposite-fold pilot density estimator.

symbols.name: \(\beta\)
symbols.def: Effective anisotropic pilot smoothness defined by \(\beta^{-1}=s_y^{-1}+d s_z^{-1}\) for \(d\ge1\).

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\)
symbols.def: Uniform pilot scale \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}=(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\).

symbols.name: \(\lambda_n\)
symbols.def: Galerkin ridge satisfying \(\lambda_n=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\downarrow0\).

symbols.name: \(T\)
symbols.def: Fixed clipping map \(T(x)=\min\{2C,\max\{c/2,x\}\}\).

symbols.name: \(\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}\)
symbols.def: Indices of tensor products of nonconstant outcome wavelets through \(J_y\) and covariate wavelets through \(J_z\); for \(d=0\), only the singleton covariate index is retained.

symbols.name: \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\)
symbols.def: Column vector \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)=(\psi^y_\lambda(y)\psi^z_\gamma(z))_{(\lambda,\gamma)\in\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}}\).

symbols.name: \(D_{J_y,J_z}\)
symbols.def: Projection dimension \(D_{J_y,J_z}=|\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}|\asymp2^{J_y+dJ_z}\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi_{J_y,J_z}\)
symbols.def: Orthogonal projection in \(L^2(dy\,dR_n)\) onto the declared anisotropic tensor features.

symbols.name: \(P_{J_y}\)
symbols.def: Orthogonal outcome-wavelet projector onto the zero-mean levels through \(J_y\).

symbols.name: \(H_y^{-1}\)
symbols.def: Outcome-wavelet negative-order reference with coefficient weight \(2^{-2j_y}\) at outcome level \(j_y\), tensored with the identity over retained covariate coordinates.

symbols.name: \(\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Projected discrepancy coefficients \(\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\Delta_n(y,z)dydR_n(z)\).

symbols.name: \(\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Arm covariance \(\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}=\operatorname{Cov}_{P_{a,n}}\{\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,1,n})\}\).

symbols.name: \(\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Two-sample covariance \(\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{0,J_y,J_z,n}+\Gamma_{1,J_y,J_z,n}\), the covariance of a foldwise contrast multiplied by \(\sqrt m\).

symbols.name: \(H_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Projected inverse-elliptic Hessian matrix with entries \(H_{\lambda\mu}=\int\Phi_\lambda(y,z)(\mathcal G_{n,z}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z))(y)dydR_n(z)\); this is one half of the second Fr\'echet derivative and hence the quadratic coefficient of the endpoint.

symbols.name: \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: One-fold whitened Hessian \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}H_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathsf K_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Normalized two-fold Hessian \(\mathsf K_{J_y,J_z,n}=K_{J_y,J_z,n}\oplus K_{J_y,J_z,n}\), because \(n(\widehat\theta-\theta)=m\sum_{e=1}^2(\widehat\theta_e-\theta)\) for the equal-weight two-fold estimator.

symbols.name: \(\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Nonzero eigenvalues of \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}\), repeated with multiplicity.

symbols.name: \(u\)
symbols.def: Positive threshold for the spectral counting function.

symbols.name: \(N_{J_y,J_z,n}(u)\)
symbols.def: Counting function \(N_{J_y,J_z,n}(u)=|\{k:\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\ge u\}|\) of the globally ordered one-fold spectrum.

symbols.name: \(v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Orthonormal eigenvectors of \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}\) corresponding to \(\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\).

symbols.name: \(\eta_{k,n}\)
symbols.def: Whitened local shift \(\eta_{k,n}=v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt{m}\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}=2^{-1/2}v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt n\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}\).

symbols.name: \(A_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Two-fold null standard-deviation constant \(A_{J_y,J_z,n}=\{2\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\}^{1/2}=2\|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\).

symbols.name: \(\xi_{e,k}\)
symbols.def: Independent standard Gaussian coordinates indexed by fold and Hessian eigenvector.

symbols.name: \(\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Boundary-wavelet projection of the arm \(a\) joint density at resolutions \((\bar J_y,\bar J_z)\), computed only from pilot fold \(I_{a,3-e}\).

symbols.name: \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Average of the two armwise covariate-marginal wavelet projections from the opposite folds.

symbols.name: \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Normalized clipping of \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}\) to fixed positive bounds.

symbols.name: \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Raw ratio \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}=\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}/\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\), defined everywhere because the marginal pilot is positive.

symbols.name: \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Conditionally normalized clipping of \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) to fixed positive bounds.

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Pilot reference density \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}=(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}+\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)})/2\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Clipping-inactive event on which both normalized raw conditional pilots and the raw marginal pilot lie strictly inside their clipping bounds.

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Ridge Galerkin inverse of the pilot weighted Neumann operator on the zero-outcome-mean subspace.

symbols.name: \(\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Observed opposite-fold projected Hessian obtained by integrating \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\) against \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Pilot conditional transport value at each covariate, computed from the two densities \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Observable one-dimensional Kantorovich derivative of \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}\) with respect to arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Pilot plug-in endpoint \(\int\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Sum of the two opposite-fold empirical covariance matrices of \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Observable whitened Hessian \((\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Observed opposite-fold first-order score for arm \(a\), including one half of the shared-marginal value score and the centered conditional Kantorovich potential.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Pilot feature mean \(\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dydz\).

symbols.name: \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Centered evaluation-fold feature \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Diagonal-free within-arm plus cross-arm quadratic correction using \(\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Equal-weight two-fold cross-fitted anisotropic second-order estimator for the \(d\ge1\) branch.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Foldwise second-order value evaluated on fold \(e\) using the opposite fold as pilot.

symbols.name: \(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: First Hoeffding projection of \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Canonical diagonal-free second Hoeffding projection of \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n\).

symbols.name: \(V_{L,n}\)
symbols.def: Linear variance constant \(V_{L,n}=n\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n})\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat V_{L,n}\)
symbols.def: Average across the two folds of the sum of the two within-arm sample variances of \(\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}\).

symbols.name: \(S_n\)
symbols.def: Triangular normalization \(S_n=A_{J_y,J_z,n}+\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}\).

symbols.name: \(B^y_{J_y,n}\)
symbols.def: Outcome-frequency truncation bias.

symbols.name: \(B^z_{J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Covariate-frequency truncation bias for \(d\ge1\).

symbols.name: \(r_{n,d}(s_z)\)
symbols.def: Degenerate quadratic estimation scale \(r_{n,d}(s_z)=n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) for \(d\ge1\), and \(r_{n,0}=n^{-1}\) for \(d=0\).

symbols.name: \(\rho_{Q,n}\)
symbols.def: Zero-to-quadratic transition radius \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) for \(d\ge1\), and \(n^{-1/2}\) for \(d=0\).

symbols.name: \(\rho_{L,n}\)
symbols.def: Quadratic-to-linear transition radius \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\) for \(d\ge1\), and \(n^{-1/2}\) for \(d=0\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\)
symbols.def: Local minimax root-mean-square scale derived in Theorems 3 and 4.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal K_{J_z}\)
symbols.def: A maximal set of interior covariate wavelets at level \(J_z\) with pairwise disjoint supports; \(M_{J_z}=|\mathcal K_{J_z}|\asymp2^{dJ_z}\).

symbols.name: \(M_{J_z}\)
symbols.def: Cardinality \(M_{J_z}=|\mathcal K_{J_z}|\asymp2^{dJ_z}\).

symbols.name: \(c_0\)
symbols.def: A fixed sufficiently small amplitude constant for the lower-bound families.

symbols.name: \(C_{\chi}\)
symbols.def: Fixed constant in the product-mixture chi-square bound.

symbols.name: \(\omega\)
symbols.def: Rademacher sign vector indexed by \(\mathcal K_{J_z}\).

symbols.name: \(\gamma_n\)
symbols.def: Lower-bound amplitude \(\gamma_n=c_0\min\{2^{-J_z(s_z+d/2)},\rho M_{J_z}^{-1/2}\}\), where \(c_0>0\) is a sufficiently small fixed constant.

symbols.name: \(b_{n,\omega}\)
symbols.def: Sign-paired wavelet amplitude \(b_{n,\omega}(z)=\gamma_n\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_{J_z}}\omega_k\psi^z_{J_z,k}(z)\).

symbols.name: \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}\)
symbols.def: Lower-bound conditional densities \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}(y,z)=1+(2a-1)b_{n,\omega}(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\).

symbols.name: \(\overline{\mathbb P}_n\)
symbols.def: Uniform Rademacher mixture of the two-arm product laws induced by \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbb P_n^0\)
symbols.def: Two-arm product law with both conditional densities equal to one.

symbols.name: \(t\)
symbols.def: Fixed-frequency amplitude for the no-covariate submodel.

symbols.name: \(q_{a,t}^{0}\)
symbols.def: No-covariate fixed-frequency density \(q_{a,t}^{0}(y)=1+(2a-1)t\cos(2\pi y)/2\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta^0_{J_y,n}\)
symbols.def: Full-sample no-covariate projected empirical-quantile estimator retaining its diagonal term.

symbols.name: \(\mathbb B\)
symbols.def: Standard Brownian bridge.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\)
symbols.def: Confidence interval returned by the mixed linear--quadratic calibration handle.

symbols.name: \(C_B\)
symbols.def: Uniform constant multiplying the anisotropic truncation-bias envelope.

symbols.name: \(\mathsf{STAR}\)
symbols.def: Student Achievement and Retention randomized experiment used by Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn to illustrate conditional-transport causal bounds.

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), the observations \(W_{a,1,n},\ldots,W_{a,n,n}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_{a,n}\) within each \(a\in\mathcal A\), and the two arm samples are independent.
The \(\mathcal Z_d\)-marginal of \(P_{a,n}\) equals \(R_n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).
For \(d\ge1\), the common marginal density satisfies \(c\le r_n(z)\le C\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_d\).
The conditional densities satisfy \(c\le q_{a,n}(y,z)\le C\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \((y,z)\in\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d\).
Each \(q_{a,n}\) belongs to the tensor anisotropic ball \(\mathcal C^{s_y,s_z}(\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d;L)\), with the \(z\)-condition omitted when \(d=0\).
The bases \(\Psi_y\) and \(\Psi_z\) are compactly supported boundary wavelets with regularities strictly greater than \(s_y+1\) and \(s_z\), respectively.
The H\"older radius satisfies \(L>1\), so the uniform density is an interior point of the declared H\"older balls.

definitions.name: Local anisotropic conditional-transport class \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}):\text{the declared sampling, common-marginal, density-bound, anisotropic-smoothness, and local-radius properties hold at indices }(n,d)\}.\]

definitions.name: Anisotropic conditional projection
definitions.construction: For \(d\ge1\), \(\Pi_{J_y,J_z}h=\sum_{(\lambda,\gamma)\in\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}}\langle h,\psi^y_\lambda\psi^z_\gamma\rangle_{L^2(dy\,dR_n)}\psi^y_\lambda\psi^z_\gamma\); for \(d=0\), retain only the outcome sum through \(J_y\).

definitions.name: Two-sample covariance whitening and normalized Hessian
definitions.construction: Form \(\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}=\operatorname{Cov}_{P_{a,n}}\{\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,1,n})\}\), \(\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{0,J_y,J_z,n}+\Gamma_{1,J_y,J_z,n}\), \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}H_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}\), and \(\mathsf K_{J_y,J_z,n}=K_{J_y,J_z,n}\oplus K_{J_y,J_z,n}\). Let \((\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n},v_{k,J_y,J_z,n})\) be the eigenpairs of the one-fold matrix, set \(\eta_{k,n}=v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt{n/2}\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}\), and set \(A_{J_y,J_z,n}=\{4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\}^{1/2}\).

definitions.name: Observable equal-weight two-fold anisotropic second-order estimator
definitions.construction: Partition each arm into deterministic folds \(I_{a,1}\) and \(I_{a,2}\), each of size \(m=n/2\). On pilot fold \(3-e\), let \(\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be the empirical boundary-wavelet joint-density projection through \((\bar J_y,\bar J_z)\), and set \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z)=\frac12\sum_{a=0}^1\int_0^1\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du\). With \(T(x)=\min\{2C,\max\{c/2,x\}\}\), define \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)=T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z))/\int T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(v))dv\), \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)/\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)\), and \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z))/\int_0^1T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z))du\). The event \(\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\) is \(c/2<\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}<2C\) and \(c/2<\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}<2C\) pointwise for both arms; clipping is inactive on this event, while normalization enforces exact conditional mass. The displayed operations keep every object defined on its complement. Put \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}=(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}+\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)})/2\) and, on the zero-outcome-mean wavelet space, \[\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}=\left[P_{J_y}\{-\partial_y(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)\partial_y)\}P_{J_y}+\lambda_n I\right]^{-1}P_{J_y}.\] Define \(\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) entrywise by \[\widehat H_{\lambda\mu}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_\lambda(y,z)\{\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dydz.\] Let \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)=W_2^2(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy,\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy)\), let \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be its observable one-dimensional Kantorovich derivative in arm \(a\), and let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}=\int\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\). The explicit first-order score is \[\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\frac12\{\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)-\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\}+\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)-\int_0^1\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du.\] Set \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), where \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\). The diagonal-free correction is \[\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\frac{1}{m(m-1)}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{i\ne j\in I_{a,e}}(X_{a,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{a,j}^{(-e)}-\frac{2}{m^2}\sum_{i\in I_{1,e}}\sum_{j\in I_{0,e}}(X_{1,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{0,j}^{(-e)}.\] Finally, \[\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+\sum_{a=0}^1\frac1m\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n},\qquad \widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}.\]

definitions.name: Pilot resolutions, ridge, and observable linear variance
definitions.construction: For \(d\ge1\), set \(\beta^{-1}=s_y^{-1}+ds_z^{-1}\), \(2^{\bar J_y}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_y(2\beta+1))}\), \(2^{\bar J_z}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_z(2\beta+1))}\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}=(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\), and \(\lambda_n=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). Let \(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) be the sum over \(a=0,1\) of the usual sample covariance of \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})\), \(i\in I_{a,3-e}\), and set \(\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\). If \(\bar s_{a,e}=m^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})\), define \[V_{L,n}=n\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}),\qquad \widehat V_{L,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{1}{m-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\{\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})-\bar s_{a,e}\}^2.\]

definitions.name: Conditional smoothness--separation rate
definitions.construction: For \(d\ge1\), define \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}\), where \(r_{n,d}(s_z)=n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\). The zero-to-quadratic boundary is \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\), and the quadratic-to-linear boundary is \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\).

definitions.name: No-covariate growing-outcome-resolution branch
definitions.construction:
When \(d=0\), define the empirical distribution function in arm \(a\) by \(\widehat F_{a,n}(y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{Y_{a,i,n}\le y\}\) and its left-continuous generalized inverse by \(\widehat Q_{a,n}(u)=\inf\{y\in[0,1]:\widehat F_{a,n}(y)\ge u\}\). Let \(V^Q_{J_y}\) be the span of all boundary scaling functions and wavelets from \(\Psi_y\) through level \(J_y\), with the constant scaling function retained, and let \(P^Q_{J_y}\) be the \(L^2[0,1]\)-orthogonal projector onto \(V^Q_{J_y}\). Define the full-sample statistic
\[
\widehat\theta^0_{J_y,n}=\int_0^1\left[P^Q_{J_y}\{\widehat Q_{1,n}-\widehat Q_{0,n}\}(u)\right]^2du .
\]
Choose \(J_y^0\) so that \(2^{J_y^0}\to\infty\), \(2^{J_y^0}=o(n)\), and \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^0}=o(n^{-1})\). The square retains its diagonal term. Define \(\mathfrak R_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}\).

definitions.name: Sign-paired conditional wavelet family
definitions.construction: For \(d\ge1\), set \(2^{J_z}\asymp n^{2/(4s_z+d)}\), \(b_{n,\omega}=\gamma_n\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_{J_z}}\omega_k\psi^z_{J_z,k}\), \(r_n(z)=1\), and \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}(y,z)=1+(2a-1)b_{n,\omega}(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\). The null member has \(b_{n,\omega}=0\).

definitions.name: Fixed-frequency no-covariate family
definitions.construction: For \(d=0\), set \(q_{a,t}^{0}(y)=1+(2a-1)t\cos(2\pi y)/2\); use the pairs \(t=0\) and \(t=c_0n^{-1/2}\) at equality, and \(t=t_0\) and \(t=t_0+c_0n^{-1/2}\) for a fixed sufficiently small \(t_0\ne0\).

definitions.name: Mixed linear--quadratic calibration handle
definitions.construction: Use the displayed cross-fitted scores \(\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}\), Hessians \(\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), and diagonal-free kernels \(\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}\); apply common Gaussian multipliers to the linear and quadratic summands while retaining their covariance; and enlarge the inverted two-sided critical region by the deterministic envelope \(C_B\{2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+\mathbf 1\{d\ge1\}2^{-2s_zJ_z}\}\). The target object is \(\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\), with no pretest or variance-threshold switch.

statements.statement: For \(q_{0,n}(y,z)=1-b(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\) and \(q_{1,n}(y,z)=1+b(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\), uniformly as \(\|b\|_{\infty}\to0\), \[\theta_n=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{\mathcal Z_d}b(z)^2dR_n(z)+O(\|b\|_{\infty}^3),\qquad D\theta_n|_{q_{0,n}=q_{1,n}}=0,\qquad \frac12D^2\theta_n[h,h]=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}h(y,z)(\mathcal G_{n,z}h(\cdot,z))(y)dydR_n(z).\] In particular, the scalar path \(q_{0,n}=1\), \(q_{1,n}=1+t b(z)\cos(2\pi y)\) has second derivative \((4\pi^2)^{-1}\int b^2dR_n\) at \(t=0\).
statements.justification: The exact coefficient fixes the Hessian convention, the lower-bound separation, and the null-law constants.
statements.gap: LinGaoBlanchetGlynn2026SmoothCOT stops at a vanishing first derivative, while GoldmanHuesmannOtto2021 supplies deterministic Poisson linearization but not this conditional statistical second variation.
statements.consumer: The sign-paired lower-bound family and the \(\mathsf{STAR}\) simulation benchmark use this coefficient.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(z\) and first let \(q(\cdot,z)\) be any common density satisfying \(c\le q\le C\).  For a zero-mass direction \(h(\cdot,z)\), put
\[
 H_h(y,z)=\int_0^y h(x,z)\,dx .
\]
The zero-mass condition gives \(H_h(0,z)=H_h(1,z)=0\).  Along the symmetric path \(q_{0,t}=q-th/2\), \(q_{1,t}=q+th/2\), the implicit equation \(F_{a,t}\{Q_{a,t}(u)\}=u\), the density lower bound, and ordinary implicit differentiation give
\[
 \dot Q_{1,0}(u,z)-\dot Q_{0,0}(u,z)
 =-\frac{H_h(Q(u,z),z)}{q(Q(u,z),z)}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Since the two quantiles coincide at \(t=0\), differentiating their squared \(L^2(0,1)\) distance once gives zero.  Differentiating twice, then changing variables \(u=F(y,z)\), gives
\[
 \frac12D^2W_2^2(q\,dy,q\,dy)[h,h]
 =\int_0^1\frac{H_h(y,z)^2}{q(y,z)}\,dy.              \tag{2}
\]
On the other hand, if \(u_h=\mathcal G_{n,z}h\), integration of the declared Neumann equation yields
\[
 q(y,z)\partial_yu_h(y,z)=-H_h(y,z).
\]
The boundary terms vanish, so
\[
 \int_0^1h u_h\,dy
 =\int_0^1q|\partial_yu_h|^2dy
 =\int_0^1\frac{H_h^2}{q}\,dy.                        \tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3), followed by integration with respect to the common marginal \(R_n\), prove the asserted first and second variations.  All divisions use \(q\ge c\), and conditioning and integration over \(z\) use the shared-marginal assumption.

For the displayed cosine pair, write \(e=b(z)/2\).  Its conditional distribution functions are
\[
 F_{1,e}(y)=y+\frac{e}{2\pi}\sin(2\pi y),\qquad
 F_{0,e}(y)=y-\frac{e}{2\pi}\sin(2\pi y).
\]
For \(|e|<1\), their derivatives are uniformly bounded away from zero.  Uniform implicit Taylor expansion of the inverses therefore gives
\[
 F_{1,e}^{-1}(u)-F_{0,e}^{-1}(u)
 =-\frac{2e}{2\pi}\sin(2\pi u)+O(|e|^2)
 =-\frac{b(z)}{2\pi}\sin(2\pi u)+O(|b(z)|^2),         \tag{4}
\]
where the remainder is uniform in \(u,z\).  Squaring (4), integrating in \(u\), and using \(\int_0^1\sin^2(2\pi u)du=1/2\) yields
\[
 W_2^2(Q_{0,n}(\cdot\mid z),Q_{1,n}(\cdot\mid z))
 =\frac{b(z)^2}{8\pi^2}+O(|b(z)|^3).                  \tag{5}
\]
The compact support of \(R_n\) turns the integrated remainder into \(O(\|b\|_\infty^3)\).  Finally, for the one-sided scalar path \(q_0=1\), \(q_1=1+t b(z)\cos(2\pi y)\), equation (2) applies with \(H_h=b(z)\sin(2\pi y)/(2\pi)\); hence the quadratic coefficient is \(\int b^2dR_n/(8\pi^2)\) and the second derivative is \(\int b^2dR_n/(4\pi^2)\).

statements.statement:
Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,ho)\), there are fixed constants \(0<c_H<C_H<\infty\) and \(0<c_\Gamma<C_\Gamma<\infty\) such that, if \(g=\sum_{(j_y,k_y,\gamma)\in\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}\psi^y_{j_y,k_y}\psi^z_\gamma\), then \[c_H\sum_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}2^{-2j_y}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}^2\le\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}g(y,z)\{\mathcal G_{n,z}g(\cdot,z)\}(y)dydR_n(z)\le C_H\sum_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}2^{-2j_y}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}^2,\] and \(c_\Gamma I\preceq\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}\preceq C_\Gamma I\). The min--max principle therefore transfers the globally ordered spectrum of the diagonal \(H_y^{-1}\) reference to \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}\): for \(2^{-2J_y}\le u\le1\) and \(1\le k\le D_{J_y,J_z}\), \[N_{J_y,J_z,n}(u)\asymp\min\{D_{J_y,J_z},2^{dJ_z}u^{-1/2}\},\qquad 
u_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\asymp\min\{1,(2^{dJ_z}/k)^2\}.\] Consequently, for \(d\ge1\), \[\|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\asymp1,\qquad \|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\asymp2^{dJ_z},\qquad  rac{\max_k|
u_{k,J_y,J_z,n}|}{\{\sum_k
u_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\}^{1/2}}\lesssim2^{-dJ_z/2}.\] The same quadratic-form comparison and anisotropic approximation give \( |B^y_{J_y,n}|\lesssim2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}\) and \( |B^z_{J_z,n}|\lesssim2^{-2s_zJ_z}\). When \(d=0\), the Hilbert--Schmidt norm remains bounded above and away from zero as \(J_y	o\infty\).
statements.justification: The min--max argument makes the spectrum canonical despite variable-coefficient mixing and determines both anisotropic tuning parameters.
statements.gap: NilesWeedBerthet2022 gives negative-order wavelet geometry for unconditional loss, but it does not separate outcome elliptic smoothing from replicated covariate directions in a conditional Hessian.
statements.consumer: The expansion, minimax rate, spectral transition, and confidence bias envelope all use these three scales.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(g\) be the displayed finite wavelet sum and, for each \(z\), let \(u_z=\mathcal G_{n,z}g(\cdot,z)\).  The Neumann boundary conditions and the zero outcome integral of every retained feature give
\[
 \langle g,u_z\rangle_{L^2(dy)}
 =\int_0^1\bar q_n(y,z)|\partial_yu_z(y)|^2dy.          \tag{1}
\]
Uniform ellipticity \(c\le\bar q_n\le C\), the variational characterization of the inverse, and the one-dimensional Poincar\'e inequality imply, with constants depending only on \(c,C\),
\[
 \langle g,\mathcal G_{n,z}g\rangle
 \asymp \|g(\cdot,z)\|_{H^{-1}(0,1)}^2.               \tag{2}
\]
For the declared boundary wavelets, regularity strictly greater than \(s_y+1>1\) gives the negative Sobolev Riesz equivalence
\[
 \|g\|_{L^2(dR_n;H^{-1}_y)}^2
 \asymp\sum_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}2^{-2j_y}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}^2. \tag{3}
\]
This equivalence follows directly by applying the antiderivative to each compactly supported outcome wavelet: its \(L^2\) norm is comparable to \(2^{-j_y}\), distinct levels have uniformly bounded overlap, and the boundary scaling functions form a fixed finite-dimensional block.  The bounds \(c\le r_n\le C\) transfer the Lebesgue tensor estimate to \(dR_n\).  Combining (1)--(3) proves the first display.

Write \(p_{a,n}=q_{a,n}r_n\) for \(d\ge1\).  If \(x\) is the coefficient vector of \(g\), then
\[
 x^\top\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}x
 =\inf_{v\in\mathbb R}\int(g-v)^2p_{a,n}\,dy\,dz.       \tag{4}
\]
Because \(\int_0^1g(y,z)dy=0\) for every \(z\),
\[
 \int(g-v)^2dy\,dz=\int g^2dy\,dz+v^2.
\]
The two density lower bounds and Parseval therefore give a fixed positive lower bound in (4), while the upper density bounds give a fixed upper bound.  For \(d=0\), the same argument uses only \(c\le q_{a,n}\le C\).  Summing the two arms proves \(c_\Gamma I\preceq\Gamma\preceq C_\Gamma I\).

Congruence by \(\Gamma^{1/2}\), (3), and the Courant--Fischer min--max formula compare the eigenvalues of \(K\) with those of the diagonal reference carrying weight \(2^{-2j_y}\).  There are \(\asymp2^{j_y+dJ_z}\) coordinates at outcome level \(j_y\).  Thus, for \(2^{-2J_y}\le u\le1\),
\[
 N(u)\asymp 2^{dJ_z}\sum_{j_y\le(1/2)\log_2(u^{-1})}2^{j_y}
 \asymp\min\{D_{J_y,J_z},2^{dJ_z}u^{-1/2}\}.           \tag{5}
\]
Inverting (5) gives \(\nu_k\asymp\min\{1,(2^{dJ_z}/k)^2\}\).  Hence
\[
 \sum_k\nu_k^2\asymp
 2^{dJ_z}+2^{4dJ_z}\sum_{k>2^{dJ_z}}k^{-4}
 \asymp2^{dJ_z},                                       \tag{6}
\]
while the largest eigenvalue is comparable to one.  Equations (5)--(6) prove all three spectral assertions and the normalized maximal-eigenvalue bound.  When \(d=0\), the same sum has no growing multiplicity and converges to a finite positive constant.

Finally, the tensor H\"older coefficient bounds implied by the declared wavelet regularity are
\[
 |\langle\Delta_n,\psi^y_{j_y,k_y}\psi^z_\gamma\rangle|
 \lesssim2^{-j_y(s_y+1/2)}2^{-j_z(s_z+d/2)}.            \tag{7}
\]
The second-order truncation remainders are quadratic in the omitted nuisance component after the first-order term has been removed.  Weighting the outcome tail in (7) by \(2^{-2j_y}\) and summing gives \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}\); summing the covariate tail gives \(2^{-2s_zJ_z}\).  These are precisely the declared components \(B^y_{J_y,n}\) and \(B^z_{J_z,n}\), proving their asserted bounds uniformly over the fixed-radius ball.

statements.statement:
For the opposite-fold estimator and the declared pilot resolutions, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\max_e\left[\|\widehat r_n^{(-e)}-r_n\|_\infty+\max_a\|\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}-q_{a,n}\|_\infty\right]=O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}),\qquad P\left(\bigcap_{e=1}^2\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\right)\to1.
\]
The clipping is inactive on that event, and conditional normalization is exact everywhere. Coercivity and the resolvent identity give
\[
\max_e\|\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-H_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}+\lambda_n).
\]
The plug-in, ridge, and operator contribution to the second-order expansion is \(O_P\{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\}+o_P(1)\{\rho_n/\sqrt n+A_{J_y,J_z,n}/n\}\). Hence it is negligible relative to the displayed expansion scale whenever
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2=o\!\left(\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n+2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}\right).
\]
If additionally \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n/m=o(1)\), then \(\max_e\|\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1)\) and \(\max_e\|\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1)\); this extra covariance condition is required only when the population triangular proxy is replaced by its observed spectral plug-in, not for the point estimator.
statements.justification: This result separates what the primitive smoothness class actually guarantees for the observable pilots from the stronger covariance condition needed only for a plug-in spectral display.
statements.gap: SmoothCOT Section 3.3 and Appendix C.4 control a first-order wavelet plug-in remainder, but they do not estimate a zero-mean Galerkin Hessian or quantify clipping, ridge, and covariance errors for a growing second-order kernel.
statements.consumer: Theorems 1--3 invoke the first three conclusions, while an implementable spectral diagnostic invokes the final covariance conclusion only at resolutions where it is feasible.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(p_{a,n}(y,z)=q_{a,n}(y,z)r_n(z)\).  Products preserve the declared anisotropic H\"older ball up to a constant depending only on \(C,L\).  At the pilot resolutions, the tensor wavelet approximation error in supremum norm is bounded by
\[
 C\{2^{-s_y\bar J_y}+2^{-s_z\bar J_z}\}\lesssim\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}. \tag{1}
\]
At any point only a fixed number of compactly supported wavelets at each terminal scale are nonzero.  Applying Bernstein's exponential-moment inequality coefficientwise and taking a union bound over \(O(2^{\bar J_y+d\bar J_z})\) coefficients gives
\[
 \max_{a,e}\|\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}-p_{a,n}\|_\infty
 +\max_e\|\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}-r_n\|_\infty
 =O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n})                     \tag{2}
\]
uniformly over the model class.  The denominators \(r_n\ge c\), the ratio identity
\[
 \frac{\widetilde p}{\widetilde r}-\frac p r
 =\frac{\widetilde p-p}{\widetilde r}
   +p\frac{r-\widetilde r}{{r\widetilde r}},            \tag{3}
\]
and (2) prove the same rate for the raw conditional pilots.  Since the true densities lie in the strict interior of the clipping bounds \(c/2,2C\), (2) implies \(P(\cap_e\mathcal E_n^{(-e)})\to1\).  Clipping and normalization are locally Lipschitz on that event and enforce positivity and unit conditional mass on its complement, proving the first two conclusions.

Let \(A_z=P_{J_y}\{-\partial_y(\bar q_n\partial_y)\}P_{J_y}\) and let \(\widehat A_z\) be its pilot analogue.  On the zero-mean subspace, ellipticity and Poincar\'e give \(A_z\succeq c_PI\) uniformly.  The variational form gives \(\|\widehat A_z-A_z\|\lesssim\|\widehat{\bar q}-\bar q\|_\infty\).  The resolvent identity
\[
 (\widehat A_z+\lambda_nI)^{-1}-A_z^{-1}
 =(\widehat A_z+\lambda_nI)^{-1}
 \{A_z-\widehat A_z-\lambda_nI\}A_z^{-1}              \tag{4}
\]
therefore has operator norm \(O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}+\lambda_n)\).  Integration against \(\widehat r_n\), using (2), proves the displayed Hessian bound.

It remains to track the population correction.  Parameterize a pair by its average density \(\bar q\) and discrepancy \(\Delta\).  Arm exchange sends \(\Delta\) to \(-\Delta\) without changing \(W_2^2\), so the functional is even in \(\Delta\).  The quantile implicit equation used in the cosine proof, twice polarized and integrated, shows on the density set \([c/2,2C]\) that the equality Hessian is Lipschitz in \(\bar q\), while its difference from the Hessian at \((\bar q,\Delta)\) is \(O(\|\Delta\|_\infty)\) as a bilinear form on the pilot error.  The anisotropic interpolation inequality implied by the declared H\"older ball and the zero outcome mass is
\[
 \|\Delta_n\|_\infty
 \lesssim \rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}.                 \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, an amplitude \(A\) at a maximum persists on outcome and covariate rectangles of side lengths \(A^{1/s_y}\) and \(A^{1/s_z}\); the zero-mass outcome antiderivative then has squared \(L^2(dR_n;L^2_y)\) norm at least a constant times \(A^{2+3/s_y+d/s_z}\).  Its norm is comparable to \(\rho_n^2\) by ellipticity, proving (5).  Taylor's identity with integral remainder therefore gives
\[
 O_P\{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+
 \rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\}.                       \tag{6}
\]
The first term is the equality third-order remainder; the second is the unequal-law Hessian mismatch.  Replacing the equality Hessian by its ridge pilot contributes \(O_P\{(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}+\lambda_n)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\}\), which is absorbed by (5) because \(\lambda_n=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\).  Sample splitting makes the remaining centered operator terms \(o_P(1)\{\rho_n/\sqrt n+A/n\}\).  This proves the proposed local-quadratic remainder and its stated negligibility condition.

For the covariance assertion, the feature covariance is uniformly bounded and uniformly positive by the spectrum proposition, and \(\|\Phi(W)\|_2^2\lesssim D_{J_y,J_z}\).  The matrix exponential-moment argument yields
\[
 \max_e\|\widehat\Gamma^{(-e)}-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 =O_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{D_{J_y,J_z}\log n}{m}}+
 \frac{D_{J_y,J_z}\log n}{m}\right)=o_P(1).            \tag{5}
\]
On the resulting fixed spectral interval, the matrix square-root map is Lipschitz.  Combining (4)--(5) in the definition of \(K\) proves \(\max_e\|\widehat K^{(-e)}-K\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1)\).

statements.statement:
Assume \(L>1\). For the sign-paired conditional wavelet construction and a sufficiently small fixed \(c_0\), every \(b_{n,\omega}\) has zero conditional mass after multiplication by \(\cos(2\pi y)\), \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}\ge c\), anisotropic H\"older norm at most \(L\), common marginal \(R_n(dz)=dz\), and inverse-elliptic radius at most \(\rho\). Its endpoint separation from the null equals
\[
\frac{\gamma_n^2M_{J_z}}{8\pi^2}\{1+o(1)\}.
\]
The uniform Rademacher mixture and the null product law satisfy
\[
\chi^2(\overline{\mathbb P}_n,\mathbb P_n^0)\le\exp\{C_{\chi}n^2\gamma_n^4M_{J_z}\}-1.
\]
At \(2^{J_z}\asymp n^{2/(4s_z+d)}\), the exponent is bounded and the separation is a fixed multiple of \(\min\{\rho^2,r_{n,d}(s_z)\}\). The fixed-frequency no-covariate construction is positive, normalized, H\"older, and has bounded product Hellinger distance for parameter increments of order \(n^{-1/2}\).
statements.justification: The converse is tied to a named finite family with every membership and testing-distance check exposed.
statements.gap: BickelRitov1988 and IngsterSuslina2003 provide quadratic-functional mixture templates, but not a two-arm conditional-density construction preserving a shared marginal and conditional normalization.
statements.consumer: The conditional minimax frontier uses the Rademacher mixture for the quadratic and zero zones, while the no-covariate recovery theorem uses the fixed-frequency branch.

statements.statement:
Let \(d\ge1\), \(J_y,J_z\to\infty\), \(D_{J_y,J_z}=o(n^2)\), and use the observable anisotropic estimator with the declared pilot tuning and studentizer. If
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2=o\!\left(\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n+2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}\right),
\]
then, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n=\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}+\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}+B^y_{J_y,n}+B^z_{J_z,n}+o_P\!\left(\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n+2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}\right).
\]
Here \(\operatorname{sd}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n})\asymp\rho_n/\sqrt n\), \(\operatorname{sd}(\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n})=A_{J_y,J_z,n}/n\), and \(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}=0\) at conditional equality. At \((J_y^*,J_z^*)\), the three projection and quadratic terms are of order \(r_{n,d}(s_z)\); the observable root-mean-square scale is
\[
\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+r_{n,d}(s_z)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2,
\]
and it reduces to \(\rho_n/\sqrt n+r_{n,d}(s_z)\) when the final two terms are of no larger order. No covariance estimate enters this point-estimator expansion.
statements.justification: The uniform expansion is the analytic bridge linking primitive density smoothness to the local linear and growing-rank quadratic experiment.
statements.gap: SmoothCOT Section 3.3 and Appendix C.4 use quadratic stability for a regular first-order wavelet CLT, while GoldmanHuesmannOtto2021 controls deterministic transport linearization; neither result supplies this observable ridge-Galerkin, anisotropic, resolution-uniform second-order expansion. LinGaoBlanchetGlynn2026COT advertises a direct nonparametric estimator and a convergence rate in verified abstract and proceedings metadata, but its formula-level theorem overlap is externally unverifiable.
statements.consumer: The spectral law, sharp rate, and mixed calibration all use this single decomposition.
statements.proof_tex:
Condition on both pilot folds.  Independence of the evaluation observations from the opposite-fold pilots follows from the sampling assumption and the deterministic split.  Apply the exact Hoeffding decomposition to each diagonal-free quadratic correction.  After averaging folds, its first projection combines with the displayed one-step score to give \(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}\), its canonical second projection is \(\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}\), and the omitted projection components are \(B^y_{J_y,n}+B^z_{J_z,n}\).  Thus the decomposition is an identity plus the pilot/operator remainder.

For the linear projection, the first variation in the cosine-second-variation lemma and uniform ellipticity show that the squared \(L^2(P_{0,n})\oplus L^2(P_{1,n})\) norm of the centered score is comparable to \(\rho_n^2\).  Independence of the two arms and the two equal folds therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n})\asymp\frac{\rho_n^2}{n}, \tag{1}
\]
with the score identically zero when \(\Delta_n=0\).

For the canonical quadratic projection, the two-sample feature contrast on one fold has covariance \(\Gamma/m\).  Whitening and diagonalizing \(K=\Gamma^{1/2}H\Gamma^{1/2}\), the exact variance formula for a diagonal-free order-two statistic gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n})
 =\frac{4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2}{n^2}\{1+o(1)\}
 =\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2}{n^2}\{1+o(1)\}.                \tag{2}
\]
The \(o(1)\) is uniform because \(D=o(n^2)\), the densities are bounded, and compact wavelet support bounds the fourth-moment contraction by \(D/n^2=o(1)\).  The spectrum proposition supplies the two deterministic bias bounds.

The proposed pilot-control lemma bounds every remaining plug-in and ridge term by
\[
 O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+
 \rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2)
 +o_P(1)\left\{\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac A n\right\}. \tag{3}
\]
Under the proposed condition, (3) is little-oh of the sum of the four displayed scales.  Combining (1)--(3) with the exact Hoeffding identity proves the proposed uniform expansion.  At the rate-balancing resolutions, the spectrum proposition and the tuning identities give
\[
 \frac A n\asymp\frac{2^{dJ_z^*/2}}n
 \asymp2^{-2s_zJ_z^*}
 \asymp2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^*}
 \asymp r_{n,d}(s_z).                                   \tag{4}
\]
Consequently \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2=o\{\rho_n/\sqrt n+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}\) makes the observable remainder negligible at that scale.  Without this last condition the same calculation gives the honest root-mean-square upper scale \(\rho_n/\sqrt n+r_{n,d}(s_z)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\).

statements.statement:
Under the proposed uniform second-order expansion, suppose additionally that \(\|\Delta_n\|_\infty\to0\) and
\[
2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}=O(S_n/n),
\qquad S_n=A_{J_y,J_z,n}+\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}.
\]
Then the \(n\)-dependent triangular approximation
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],\mathcal L\left[\frac{1}{S_n}\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\{(\xi_{e,k}+\eta_{k,n})^2-(1+\eta_{k,n}^2)\}\right]\right)\to0
\]
holds, where the spectrum is repeated twice, \(A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2=4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\), and \(\eta_{k,n}=2^{-1/2}v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt n\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}\). At equality all shifts vanish; if \(J_z\to\infty\), then \(n\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}/A_{J_y,J_z,n}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\). A centered Gaussian-chaos limit is asserted only along subsequences for which the padded ordered arrays \((\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}/A_{J_y,J_z,n})_k\) and \((\eta_{k,n})_k\) converge in \(\ell^2\). If \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n/m=o(1)\), the population kernel may be replaced by the average observed kernel. Separately, at fixed unequal laws, if \(\widehat V_{L,n}/V_{L,n}\to_P1\), \(\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}/A_{J_y,J_z,n}\to\infty\), and the displayed bias and remainder are \(o(\sqrt{V_{L,n}/n})\), then
\[
\frac{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n}{\sqrt{\widehat V_{L,n}/n}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Thus the triangular noncentral representation is equality-local, whereas the regular Gaussian conclusion remains valid at fixed unequal laws.
statements.justification: The theorem makes the triangular Gaussian-quadratic proxy primary, records the split constants, and limits fixed-chaos claims to genuine spectral convergence subsequences.
statements.gap: SmoothCOT Theorem 3.2, Remark 3.2, and Appendix C.4 stop at the regular CLT and a rate statement at equality; DelBarrioGineUtzet2005 is unconditional, RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2016 begins with a supplied kernel, and AgarwalLuedtke2026 fixes entropic damping.
statements.consumer: The result determines critical values near equality and identifies when a Gaussian approximation is legitimate despite first-order degeneracy.

statements.statement:
Assume \(L>1\). For every \(d\ge1\), there are constants \(0<c_1<C_1<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that
\[
c_1\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\le\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}
\]
\[
\le C_1\min\!\left[\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\right],
\]
where \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\). The observable upper bound uses \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y^*,J_z^*,n}\), or the zero estimator when \(\rho\lesssim\rho_{Q,n}\). The quadratic and zero-zone lower bounds hold on the explicit sign-paired family in the mixture-check lemma. In the zone \(\rho\gg n^{-1/2}\), extending \(q_{a,t}^{0}\) constantly in \(z\) and comparing \(t=c_0\rho\) with \(t=c_0\rho+c_0n^{-1/2}\) supplies the regular \(\rho n^{-1/2}\) lower bound. The bracket is matched whenever
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2
=O\{\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}.
\]
In this matching region the intrinsic quadratic elbow is \(s_z=d/4\): when \(s_z>d/4\), \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) and \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\) delimit zero, quadratic, mixed, and regular zones; when \(s_z\le d/4\), the quadratic term prevents a positive-variance root-\(n\) rate uniformly over the class. Outside the matching region, the displayed two-sided bracket is the conclusion and its tightness is not asserted.
statements.justification: The theorem recomputes the elbow from canonical ordered-spectrum bounds, exposes the pilot-feasibility restriction on the observable upper bound, and matches it with an explicit converse.
statements.gap: SmoothCOT Section 3.3, Theorem 3.2, Remark 3.2, and Appendix C.4 do not state an equality-local minimax frontier. LinGaoBlanchetGlynn2026COT advertises a direct nonparametric conditional-OT estimator and a convergence rate in its arXiv abstract and AISTATS metadata, but formula-level overlap is externally unverifiable because the proceedings theorem text was inaccessible; no particular comparator rate or non-overlap is claimed.
statements.consumer: Analysts tuning conditional causal bounds can distinguish whether covariate smoothness, rather than outcome smoothness, blocks regular inference.

statements.statement:
Assume \(L>1\). When \(d=0\), use the no-covariate growing-outcome-resolution construction rather than setting \(d=0\) in the conditional tuning rule. Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}\asymp\mathfrak R_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}.
\]
At equality under the uniform density, the full-sample bias-retaining estimator has the exact benchmark
\[
n\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}\Rightarrow2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{2}{\pi^2k^2}\xi_{1,k}^2,
\]
where \(J_y^0\to\infty\), \(2^{J_y^0}=o(n)\), and \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^0}=o(n^{-1})\). Subtracting \(2\sum_{k\le2^{J_y^0}}(\pi^2k^2)^{-1}/n\) yields the centered chaos. Thus the outcome resolution genuinely grows, the quadratic scale is \(n^{-1}\), and \(\rho_{Q,n}=\rho_{L,n}=n^{-1/2}\). This is the two-sample specialization of the del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet weighted quantile-process law.
statements.justification: A separate full-sample estimator is necessary to recover the classical two-sample constant rather than a split-sample direct-sum surrogate.
statements.gap: delBarrioGineUtzet2005 gives the unconditional quantile-process limit but not its role as the \(d=0\) branch of a conditional smoothness--degeneracy frontier.
statements.consumer: The result is the required sanity check and supplies exact simulation critical values when no covariate adjustment is used.

statements.statement: Can the mixed linear--quadratic calibration handle construct \(\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\) such that \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{0\le\rho\le1}\inf_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\}\ge1-\alpha,\] with expected half-width of order \(\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\) for pilot-feasible \(d\ge1\), order \(\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\) for \(d=0\), and the regular Gaussian width implied by SmoothCOT Theorem 3.2 at each fixed unequal law? The construction must derive uniform spectral-tail, anti-concentration, multiplier-coupling, observable pilot-Hessian, covariance, and anisotropic bias-envelope control from the primitive model class.
statements.justification: Uniform calibration is the genuine unresolved step needed to report one interval without pretesting equality.
statements.gap: ChenFang2019 treats fixed second-order maps, SturmaDrtonLeung2024 Gaussianizes incomplete U-statistics, and AgarwalLuedtke2026 retains fixed entropic damping; none controls a growing unregularized anisotropic Hessian and two bias tails together.
statements.consumer: A positive answer gives one defensible uncertainty report for the \(\mathsf{STAR}\) conditional bound across equality and fixed alternatives.

sampling_model.design: Two independent randomized treatment-arm samples, each of even size \(n=2m\), with deterministic equal folds of size \(m\).
sampling_model.units: Observations are \(W_{a,i,n}=(Y_{a,i,n},Z_{a,i,n})\), with scalar outcome support \([0,1]\) and covariate support \([0,1]^d\).
sampling_model.treatment: Randomized arm membership directly samples the two potential-outcome marginals.
sampling_model.overlap: Propensity overlap is not used; the arm laws share the marginal \(R_n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For \(d\ge1\), opposite-fold joint and marginal wavelet projections are conditionally normalized and clipped to fixed positive bounds. Their averaged conditional density enters a zero-outcome-mean ridge Galerkin inverse, which defines the observed Hessian, first-order score, diagonal-free kernel, and foldwise variance estimator even off the clipping-inactive event. For \(d=0\), the separate branch uses the full empirical quantile processes.

tldr: For \(d\ge1\), conditional squared Wasserstein distance has an anisotropic boundary geometry: inverse ellipticity smooths outcome frequencies while covariate resolution replicates the ordered spectrum. A min--max comparison gives Hilbert--Schmidt norm \(\asymp2^{dJ_z/2}\), outcome bias \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}\), and covariate bias \(2^{-2s_zJ_z}\). A fully observed two-fold statistic uses clipped-and-normalized opposite-fold density pilots, a ridge Galerkin inverse, explicit first-order scores, and a diagonal-free second-order kernel. In the pilot-feasible smoothness region, balancing the three scales yields local rate \(\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\) and elbow \(s_z=d/4\), matched by the sign-paired converse; the limit statement is an \(n\)-dependent Gaussian-quadratic approximation, with chaos only under \(\ell^2\) spectral convergence. The separate \(d=0\) branch recovers the two-sample del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet law and \(n^{-1}\) scale. Uniform mixed-regime calibration remains open.

project_justification.gap: SmoothCOT Section 3.3, Theorem 3.2, Remark 3.2, and Appendix C.4 stop at a regular CLT and faster-than-root-\(n\) equality statement. Existing unconditional Wasserstein laws, changing-kernel theory, fixed-entropic causal transport, and the direct-estimation COT abstract do not provide a verified observable equality-local anisotropic frontier.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a primitive smoothness-by-equality frontier that separates outcome elliptic smoothing from covariate rank and also recovers the unconditional \(d=0\) benchmark with the correct estimator and constants.
project_justification.fill: The project derives canonical ordered-spectrum and bias bounds, constructs the foldwise clipped ridge-Galerkin statistic, states the normalized triangular experiment and regular studentization with exact split constants, matches the pilot-feasible rate using a checked sign-paired wavelet family, and isolates honest all-regime calibration as the unresolved node.

related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's SmoothCOT Section 3.3 gives quadratic stability, Theorem 3.2 gives the regular Gaussian law, Remark 3.2 records faster-than-root-\(n\) convergence at equality, and Appendix C.4 proves the CLT; the mixed triangular theorem strictly tightens that scalar randomized-arm specialization. Their AISTATS 2026 paper, verified only through its arXiv abstract and proceedings metadata, advertises a direct consistent nonparametric conditional-OT value estimator and a convergence rate. Formula-level overlap with the equality-local frontier remains externally unverifiable because its proceedings theorem text was inaccessible, so it is treated only as informing the project. Goldman, Huesmann, and Otto motivate inverse-elliptic linearization. Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart inform changing-kernel approximation. Del Barrio, Gin\'e, and Utzet provide the weighted quantile-process law recovered by the separate \(d=0\) branch. Chen and Fang motivate derivative-aware calibration, and Sturma, Drton, and Leung inform multiplier coupling. Agarwal and Luedtke analyze fixed-entropic causal transport. Niles-Weed and Berthet provide negative-order wavelet geometry; Manole and Niles-Weed provide unconditional separation-sensitive rates. Goldfeld, Kato, Nietert, and Rioux treat fixed Gaussian smoothing. Neykov, Wasserman, Kim, and Balakrishnan develop multiresolution conditional Wasserstein testing. Bickel and Ritov and Ingster and Suslina inform the explicit sign-mixture converse.
technical_internal_limitation: The cosine witness reduces one lower-bound channel to a covariate quadratic functional, but the observable upper expansion still requires uniform control of a density-dependent ridge Galerkin inverse. The optimal sup-norm pilot rate makes the advertised \(s_z\)-driven upper frontier available only when \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3=o(r_{n,d}(s_z))\). Full operator-norm covariance estimation additionally requires \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n=o(m)\) and is used only for an observed spectral proxy, not for the point estimator.
honest_scope: The model has scalar compactly supported outcomes, equal randomized arm sizes, a shared covariate marginal, positive anisotropic H\"older densities, and known smoothness. The sharp conditional upper and lower frontier is stated for \(d\ge1\) only in the explicit pilot-feasible region; outside it the Rademacher lower bound remains, but no observable upper rate is claimed. The primary limit result is triangular, and a fixed Gaussian-chaos limit requires \(\ell^2\) convergence of normalized spectra and shifts. The \(d=0\) result uses a separate full-sample empirical-quantile branch. Adaptation, multivariate outcomes, observational propensity estimation, observed spectral plug-in at high dimension, and uniform mixed calibration are open.
